segments.summary: Reviewed registration, conditional prompt context, status/unregister lifecycle, provider isolation, canonical coordination authority, rationale, and update cadence. Exact contracts are strong; abnormal termination, idempotency, delivery loss, and staleness remain material adversarial gaps.

Reviewed event extraction, cross-provider scenarios, runner isolation, placement notes, crew canon, and retired gap-era guidance. Untrusted extraction and wait liveness are under-specified; isolation, parent authority, attribution, and retirement boundaries are explicit.

Reviewed crew caps, delegated lifecycle, GUI authority, future Assistant guardrails, templates, template examples, and performance metrics. Admission and projection boundaries are exact; lifecycle seam testing, template data governance, and metric truth/privacy remain gaps.

Reviewed future learning, quota/tier scheduling, user reorder, crew-aware PRD hints, JSON examples, interview crew uses, and research coverage. Governance deferrals are explicit; learning privacy, queue fairness/races, and schema ownership remain unresolved.

Reviewed interview/execution separation, rationale and comparator evidence, mirror authority, AgentMessage and MessageType examples, and board context/schema ownership. Noncanonical evidence is well fenced; payload safety and schema migration remain cross-owner seams.

Reviewed routing, help/decision/conflict examples, orchestrator monitoring, GUI insights, and prompt injection. Examples are safely nonbinding, while routing authorization, conflict resolution, monitoring oracles, GUI truth, and prompt-injection safety are substantial gaps.

Reviewed prompt example status, relevance filters, threading, lifecycle/retention, communicator paths, post validation, and platform display formatting. Canonical boundaries are preserved; leakage, graph integrity, retention privacy, and trusted-write validation require closure.

Reviewed output-command integration, insight derivation, benefit rationale, operational mitigations, checklist evidence, GUI visualization, and concurrent-write atomicity. Output authenticity, operational completeness, insight freshness, and safe GUI behavior are gaps; canonical append/CAS atomicity is explicit.
